mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) indicates elevated inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and increases the risk-free rate, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL is above the 75th percentile of its historical range (2010-2024), or the rank correlation between CPIAUCSL and 20-day returns is less than 0.05 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate below 4.5% signals an easing monetary policy, which reduces discount rates and increases risk appetite, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 4.5%, or the rank correlation between FEDFUNDS (below 4.5%) and 20-day returns is less than 0.05 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low unemployment (UNRATE < 3.5%) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 310) indicates an overheating economy, triggering aggressive monetary tightening by the Fed, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE < 3.5% and CPIAUCSL > 310, or the rank correlation between the interaction signal and returns is less than 0.05 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion characterized by high industrial production (INDPRO > 100) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%), the economy is overextended, leading to a higher probability of a market correction and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO > 100 and UNRATE < 4.0%, or the rank correlation between the regime signal and returns is less than 0.05 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong housing market activity (HOUST > 1300) signals robust consumer demand and economic expansion, which supports corporate earnings growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where HOUST > 1300, or the rank correlation between HOUST and 20-day returns is less than 0.05 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust economic activity and strong corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO is above its 50th percentile, or the rank correlation between INDPRO and 60-day returns is less than 0.05 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4.0%) signals a tight labor market, which increases the risk of wage-driven inflation and forces the Fed to maintain restrictive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE < 4.0%, or the rank correlation between UNRATE and 20-day returns is less than 0.05 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong consumer spending (RSAFS > 700000) indicates robust economic activity and positive business sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where RSAFS > 700000, or the rank correlation between RSAFS and 5-day returns is less than 0.05 in any 3-year rolling window.
